title: Feeling green
caption: A green-lit ALMA antenna under the Milky Way, Chajnantor Plateau
celestial: Landscape photograph; the source does not name the site

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: An artificial green glow lights up one of the antennas of the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) as it observes, with the Milky Way above. ALMA has 66 antennas in all, and the photograph, by Babak Tafreshi, is titled Feeling green.

The array stands on the Chajnantor plateau in the Chilean desert, more than 5000 meters above sea level. At that height the air is dry and the atmosphere is thin, and those conditions give an excellent view into the Universe. They make the plateau an ideal home for a telescope as sensitive as this one.

Each antenna is a dish that collects millimeter and submillimeter light, and the signals from many antennas are combined so that they act together as one telescope. The green light on the dish is artificial. It is not produced by the antenna's observations, which record light that no eye can see.

understand.summary: A ground-based landscape photograph by Babak Tafreshi for ESO, taken in visible light. The colors are those the camera recorded, including an artificial green light on the antenna.
understand.eye: The camera records visible light, while the antenna itself observes millimeter and submillimeter light that the eye cannot see.
